lines.text: Someone on your call says one sentence. Let's follow it through LokalBot.
First it's only sound: two tracks, your microphone and the call app's audio.
When the call ends, a speaker model marks who spoke when.
A speech model turns the sound into words, each one pinned to its moment.
A language model reads the whole transcript and writes the notes: decisions, action items, open questions.
An embedding model files it by meaning, beside a keyword index, in one database.
Days later you start typing, and a model built for speed finishes the sentence.
And only if you allow it, your coding agent can ask for it too.
One sentence, five models, under ten gigabytes. All of it running on your Mac.
LokalBot. Local by default, free and open source.
